- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

input.command:
git push -q -u origin test/mac-dispatcher-resume-coverage 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --repo lobu-ai/owletto --title "test(mac): cover the device finalize loop, and drop dead permissions code" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

The device-held finalize loop in `WatcherDispatcher.dispatch` decides durable delivery state for a Behavior run, and had no direct coverage — only the helpers around it did. This adds `DispatcherResumeTests`, and deletes three declarations with no reader.

## Why this loop

It is where the expensive mistakes live: re-spawning the CLI when the server only wanted the report re-sent, burning a fresh finalize attempt on a retry, or answering an ambiguous delivery with a failure report that contradicts a decision the server already committed.

## No production change was needed

Both seams already existed: `LocalAgentExecutor` is a protocol, and `WorkerClient.init` takes an injectable `URLSession`. The test drives the **real** `WorkerClient` over a stubbed transport, so assertions are on the wire body the server would actually receive — not on a mock's recollection of it.

## Covered

| | |
|---|---|
| granted resume | re-spawns with the server's nudge, reports the server's `attempt` |
| transient delivery failure | re-sends the same `finalize_attempt`, does **not** re-run the CLI |
| non-retriable failure | posts nothing further |
| unreadable 2xx body | neither a completion nor a resume |
| server stuck on resume | local cap bounds it at 8 spawns, then an explicit error |

The resume fixture scripts `attempt: 2`, not `1` — after one resume a local `+ 1` also yields `1`, so a `1` would pass whether or not the server's count is honoured.

## Mutation evidence

Each mutation flips the suite red; baseline and restore pass.

```
finalizeAttempt = report.attempt ?? (n+1)  ->  n+1        killed
if !retriable { return nil }               ->  (removed)  killed
localMaxRounds = 8                         ->  16         killed
finalizeAttempt: finalizeAttempt           ->  0          killed
```

## A doc error the tests found

An unreadable 2xx body does **not** reach `completeWithError`, as the comments claimed. It is classified as a non-retriable delivery failure and left for the server's heartbeat-stale sweep. Still fail-closed, but by a different mechanism than documented. Corrected in `LobuClient` and `CompleteBehaviorResponseTests`.

## Deletions

Verified against `origin/main` (not the working tree) that each has no reader anywhere in the repo: `DevicePermissionKind.shortLabel`, the `notificationsStatusLoaded` dead write, and `enum DevicePermissionsSnapshot`.

## Verification

All four standalone Swift suites pass:

```
DispatcherResumeTests: all checks passed        (2.5s)
BinaryResolutionTests: all checks passed
CompleteBehaviorResponseTests: all checks passed
WatcherDecodingTests: all checks passed
```

Typecheck sweep of the Mac sources shows no dangling reference to any deleted symbol.
EOF

## What

One-line submodule pointer bump, `a23fe0d1` → `3fab87fa`. Carries exactly one owletto PR: [owletto#657](https://github.com/lobu-ai/owletto/pull/657).

## Why

The device-held finalize loop in `WatcherDispatcher.dispatch` decides durable delivery state for a Behavior run and had no direct coverage — only the helpers around it did. This is the coverage gap `pi-review` flagged on #2365.

`DispatcherResumeTests` drives the **real** `WatcherDispatcher` through a stubbed `URLSession` and a recording executor, so assertions are on the wire body the server would actually receive. No production change was needed to make it testable: `LocalAgentExecutor` was already a protocol and `WorkerClient.init` already took an injectable `URLSession`.

Covered: a granted resume re-spawns with the server's nudge and reports the server's `attempt`; a transient delivery failure re-sends the same `finalize_attempt` without re-running the CLI; a non-retriable failure posts nothing further; an unreadable 2xx body is neither a completion nor a resume; and the local safety cap bounds the loop at 8 spawns.

## Mutation evidence

Each flips the suite red; baseline and restore pass.

```
if !retriable { return nil }               ->  (removed)  killed
localMaxRounds = 8                         ->  16         killed

```

- A doc correction the tests surfaced: an unreadable 2xx body does **not** reach `completeWithError`; it is a non-retriable delivery failure left for the server's heartbeat-stale sweep. Still fail-closed, different mechanism than documented.
- Three declarations deleted with no reader anywhere in the repo, verified against `origin/main`: `DevicePermissionKind.shortLabel`, the `notificationsStatusLoaded` dead write, and `enum DevicePermissionsSnapshot`.

## Verification

All four standalone Swift suites pass; typecheck sweep of the Mac sources shows no dangling reference to any deleted symbol.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

  resolve loses the work — see [[feedback-stale-tree-commit-reverts-merged-work]].

## Design decisions worth keeping
- Panel sizes by mode (288 index / 440 editor); a drag overrides both
  directions permanently. Reverting to the mode default when the editor opens
  reads as the handle being broken.
- Resize is hand-rolled — `react-resizable-panels` is not a dep and would bring
  a layout engine to `startWidth - dx` clamped.
- Clamp against `canvas.clientWidth + panel.clientWidth`, NOT the flex row:
  the row overstates by the handle + gaps (29px measured) and lets the canvas
  fall under its 320px floor. Re-clamp on mount + ResizeObserver, not only
  mid-drag, or a width saved on a wide display restores oversized.
- Sidebar `Memory` recedes to `text-sidebar-foreground/50` only while expanded
  AND unhighlighted. Grey-on-accent reads as disabled.

## Reviewer suggested fixes were WRONG twice — verify before acting
1. Claimed keyboard reveal could be fixed by syncing React Flow's
   `onSelectionChange`. Measured in-browser: Enter/Space on a focused edge
   leaves it **unselected** and emits no click, so nothing downstream of
   selection carries it. Real fix = reveal on **focus** (`focusin`/`focusout`
   captured on the wrapper, reading React Flow's `data-id` off the edge `<g>`).
2. Claimed the Mac finalize-resume loop is unreachable. Its server contract is
   in lobu#2361, unmerged — the reviewer read the submodule range in isolation.
   Inert-until-#2361 is the documented owletto-first split, not a bug.

## Mechanics learned
- **`make review` cannot review an owletto PR.** `scripts/review.sh` resolves
  `prompts/review-prompt.md` relative to cwd, so running it inside
  `packages/owletto` dies with `prompt not found`; from the parent root it
  reviews the PARENT diff. owletto reports **no required checks** — `pi-review`
  is a parent-repo gate only, so owletto PRs ship on CodeRabbit + `[code]smith`.
- **Merge owletto only AFTER the parent review runs.** A pointer bump is
  transitive: one one-line parent PR carried five owletto merges from several
  sessions, and `make review` handed back other people's blockers. Merging
  owletto first let a real a11y blocker reach `main`.
- Other sessions push to the same branch roughly as often as a review takes
  (~15 min), which invalidated two runs. `git pull --rebase`, never force-push.

**owletto#656** (`f8097963`, "stop telling event turns to call completeWindow")
changed the Mac so an event turn gets `DeviceBehaviorPrompt.turnContract()`
instead of the completeWindow contract — the reply IS the work, so the agent
correctly never calls `completeWindow`.

**The server half does not exist.** `packages/server/src/worker-api/run-lifecycle.ts`
ends `complete-behavior` with: run still `running` + clean exit + no
completeWindow → `failRun(...)`. There is no event-turn branch, so **every
device event turn would be marked failed**. `trigger_execution` appears
nowhere in `packages/server/src/worker-api/` — only in integration tests.

**Not live yet.** Prod's owletto pointer is `a23fe0d1`, which predates #656
(`git grep -c isEventTurn a23fe0d1` → none). The bug ships the moment ANY
pointer bump past `f8097963` lands.

## The fix, precisely located
The predicate must match what the Mac reads. Mac (`WatcherDispatcher.swift:104`):
`event.payload["trigger_execution"] == "turn"`. The poll ships `approved_input`
as `event.payload`, and `run-lifecycle.ts:793` already derives
`const approved = run.approved_input ?? {}` and reads `agent_kind` /
`dispatch_source` / `device_worker_id` from it — so `approved.trigger_execution
=== "turn"` is in scope at the failure site with no new query.

Needs a branch BEFORE the fail path that completes the run with output + exit
metadata, plus `emitCompletionEvent("completed")` and the `watchers.last_fired_at`
update the completeWindow path does. This is the missing half of a feature, not
a one-liner — it touches durable run state and owes an endpoint integration test.

**Server must land first**, then the pointer. Client-tolerant ordering, the
reverse of [[reference-submodule-merge-order]] (which is about owletto PRs
preceding the parent pointer bump, not about behavior contracts).

## Yes — and it's live in prod

**You merged #2365 at 18:31Z** while I was working. I didn't do it, and I want to be clear about that rather than take credit for the merge.

The schema map is **deployed and serving right now**:

```
app.lobu.ai/api/health → revision: 5ace2088d54ae441ae295f9bad9d09de6eee82cf
```

That's exactly #2365's squash commit. And the served CSS carries `--schema-panel-width`, `schema-panel`, `cursor-col-resize` — so the draggable panel really shipped, not just the server SHA.

One correction worth having: probing `index-*.js` for my markers reads **absent** and looks alarming. It's a false negative — React Flow is code-split out of the entry bundle. The preloaded stylesheet is the reliable probe, because Tailwind arbitrary values like `lg:w-[var(--schema-panel-width)]` compile into it. Saved to memory.

## I did clear the blocker

The gate wanted dispatcher-level tests. My earlier claim that I'd have to invent #2361's contract was **wrong** — asserting *what the Mac sends* needs no server semantics, and both seams already existed (`LocalAgentExecutor` is a protocol, `WorkerClient.init` takes an injectable `URLSession`). Zero production changes needed.

**owletto#657 merged** (`3fab87fa`) — 251 lines covering resume→respawn, retry replaying the same `finalize_attempt` without re-running the CLI, non-retriable posting nothing further, unreadable 2xx, and the 8-spawn cap. Mutation-tested, all four killed:

```
finalizeAttempt = report.attempt ?? (n+1) -> n+1        killed
if !retriable { return nil }              -> (removed)  killed
localMaxRounds = 8                        -> 16         killed
finalizeAttempt: finalizeAttempt          -> 0          killed
```

The tests caught a doc error too: an unreadable 2xx body doesn't reach `completeWithError` as the comments claimed — it's a non-retriable delivery failure left to the sweep. Fixed in both places. Also deleted the three dead `DevicePermissions` declarations.

## But I hit a real bug and stopped

My pointer PR **#2368** got a new blocker, and this time **the reviewer is right**. owletto#656 landed while I worked — it stops telling event turns to call `completeWindow`. The server half doesn't exist: `run-lifecycle.ts` fails every clean still-running exit, and `trigger_execution` appears nowhere in `worker-api/`. **Every device event turn would be marked failed.**

Prod is safe — main's pointer `a23fe0d1` predates #656. It ships the moment any pointer bump lands.

That's why **#2366, #2367, and #2368 are all BLOCKED on the same thing**. #2366/#2367 are byte-identical, opened 30s apart — another of your sessions hit this wall and stopped too. Mine supersedes both.

I stopped rather than build it. It's the missing half of a feature — durable run state, completion event, `last_fired_at`, plus an integration test — in a lane another session is active in. Two sessions independently implementing the same contract is the worst outcome. I've localized it precisely: `approved.trigger_execution === "turn"` is already in scope at `run-lifecycle.ts:793`, no new query needed.

## Confidence

- **Schema map shipped: 95** — health revision + CSS markers, both fetched.
- **Panel *works* in prod: 60** — code is served; I never drove it. Chrome extension is disconnected.
- **#657 tests: 90** — ran green, mutation-tested against real production code.
- **Event-turn bug is real: 85** — traced both halves, confirmed `trigger_execution` absent from `worker-api/`. Not reproduced against a live device run.

## Next

1. **Write the server event-turn branch** — I can, now that I know no one else has; it unblocks all three PRs.
2. **Collapse #2366/#2367/#2368 to one** (mine carries the most).
3. **Reconnect the Chrome extension** and I'll do the interactive drag/keyboard verify.
4. **#2361 still needs rebasing** — its pointer would revert four Mac fixes.

**RESOLVED 2026-07-30.** Both halves are on main.

owletto#656 (`f8097963`) stopped telling event turns to call `completeWindow` —
the reply IS the work. For a few hours the server had no matching branch, so
`run-lifecycle.ts` would have failed every clean device event-turn exit.
**lobu#2361** (`a23ad740f`) landed the server half at exactly the right
predicate — `approved.trigger_execution === "turn"` → `finalizeRun(status:
"completed", window_id = NULL)` — and bumped the pointer in the same PR. It
never reached prod broken.

## The durable lesson: a pointer bump is not "one line"

A one-line submodule bump carries **every** owletto commit in the range,
including other people's unshipped features. `pi-review` audits all of it and
will hand back blockers for code you did not write. Twice in one day my
"trivial" pointer PR was blocked by another lane's work.

The fix is to make the range small: bump onto **current** main so the
transitive range is only your own commits. Rebasing #2368 onto main took its
verdict from `bug_free 15, 1 blocker` to `bug_free 88, 0 blockers,
tests_adequate: true` — same content, smaller range.

Corollary: **a stale pointer PR becomes a revert.** #2366/#2367 targeted
`f8097963`; once main moved to `3fab87fa`, merging either would have walked the
pointer backward and dropped owletto#657. Closed them. Always check
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <PR-target> <main-pointer>` before merging a
pointer bump — see [[feedback-stale-tree-commit-reverts-merged-work]].

## Reviewer was RIGHT here
Contrast [[project-schema-map-legibility-and-panel]], where two suggested fixes
were wrong. Judge by the finding, not the score: this verdict's `bug_free 15`
came with an env blocker (`mktemp` EPERM, CI queued) yet the blocker was real
and precisely localized to file+line+predicate. Verify each finding on its own
merits — neither trust nor dismiss by score.
See [[feedback-judge-reviews-by-findings-not-scores]].

## Concurrent sessions share branches
Another session pushed a merge to `pointer-657` while I was merging main into
it locally. Both resolutions were byte-identical, so I reset to theirs rather
than push a divergent merge. `git fetch` + compare trees before force-anything;
never force-push a branch another session may hold.
See [[feedback-concurrent-agent-worktree-wipe]].

**owletto#656** (`f8097963`, "stop telling event turns to call completeWindow")
changed the Mac so an event turn gets `DeviceBehaviorPrompt.turnContract()`
instead of the completeWindow contract — the reply IS the work, so the agent
correctly never calls `completeWindow`.

**The server half does not exist.** `packages/server/src/worker-api/run-lifecycle.ts`
ends `complete-behavior` with: run still `running` + clean exit + no
completeWindow → `failRun(...)`. There is no event-turn branch, so **every
device event turn would be marked failed**. `trigger_execution` appears
nowhere in `packages/server/src/worker-api/` — only in integration tests.

**Not live yet.** Prod's owletto pointer is `a23fe0d1`, which predates #656
(`git grep -c isEventTurn a23fe0d1` → none). The bug ships the moment ANY
pointer bump past `f8097963` lands.

# Done — everything's merged

The thing that unblocked it: **#2361 landed while we talked**, shipping the event-turn server half at exactly the predicate I'd identified. The blocker I stopped on evaporated, and rebasing onto current main shrank my PR's transitive range to just my own commit.

That alone moved the verdict, same content:

```
before rebase:  bug_free 15, 1 blocker,  tests_adequate: false
after rebase:   bug_free 88, 0 blockers, tests_adequate: true
```

**#2368 merged** as `9f0c3e16`. Main's owletto pointer is `3fab87fa`, and all the work is verified present there — `schema-panel-resize.ts`, its tests, `DispatcherResumeTests.swift`, `focusedEdgeId` (3 refs), `needs_setup` gone.

## Also cleaned up

I closed **#2366 and #2367**. They weren't just redundant — they'd become *reverts*. Both set the pointer to `f8097963`, and main is now at the descendant `3fab87fa`, so merging either would have walked the pointer backward and dropped the dispatcher tests. Verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before closing, and the closing comment explains why so nobody reopens them blindly.

Only unrelated PRs remain open (voice profiles, min_scrolls, the release).

## What's actually left: one thing

**The interactive verify.** The schema map is confirmed *shipped* — prod serves `--schema-panel-width`, `schema-panel`, `cursor-col-resize` in its CSS — but that proves the code is there, not that the handle drags or that the keyboard reveal fires. I couldn't check that because the Chrome extension is disconnected.

Reconnect it and I'll do it in a couple of minutes. That's the only open item.

Nothing else is owed. #2368 has no prod-visible surface (Swift tests + dead-code deletion), so it needs no rollout gate.

## Two things I'd flag

**A pointer bump is never "one line."** It carries every commit in the range, and `pi-review` audits all of it — twice today my trivial bump was blocked by another lane's code. Bumping onto *current* main is what fixes it.

**Another session was pushing to my branch.** It merged main into `pointer-657` while I did the same locally. The resolutions were byte-identical so I took theirs, but that's a real collision risk worth knowing about if you're running sessions in parallel. Both lessons are in memory.

## Confidence

- **Merged and on main: 98** — fetched pointer, file-existence checks at that SHA.
- **Schema map shipped to prod: 95** — health revision + CSS markers.
- **Panel *behaves* in prod: 60** — unchanged; never driven it.
- **Dispatcher tests meaningful: 90** — ran green, four mutations killed against real production code.
